security_audit.summary: All 17 static findings are false positives: nine concern Markdown formatting, and eight concern public HTTPS endpoints supporting the documented research workflow. No evidence found of command execution, credential collection, exfiltration, or prompt injection in SKILL.md. This review covers the supplied instructions, not the implementation or behavior of the external service.

content.user_title: Research Stock and ETF Risk with Redstone Markets
content.value_statement: Comparing historical returns and risk across stocks, ETFs, and portfolios requires consistent metrics. This skill directs assistants to Redstone Markets tools and public pages for those comparisons.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve stock or ETF total returns, dividend yield, and risk metrics, including drawdown, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino, beta, and alpha versus SPY.
Compare two to five stocks or ETFs with performance metrics and correlations.
Backtest hypothetical weighted portfolios containing two to twenty holdings with quarterly rebalancing.
Screen stocks or ETFs ranked by a return, risk, or yield metric.
Search shared and model portfolios and retrieve an individual portfolio.
Request public ticker, comparison, portfolio, screener, guide, and methodology pages as Markdown using an HTTP Accept header.
limitations: Data is end-of-day, not real-time; the instructions describe US-listed stock and ETF coverage rather than every security.
The skill provides instructions only; requests require network access and a compatible MCP client or page-fetching tool.
Comparisons support two to five securities; portfolio backtests support two to twenty holdings and quarterly rebalancing.
Results describe historical performance, not predictions or investment advice; external service behavior was not verified in this review.

use_cases.title: Compare ETF History
use_cases.description: Compare candidate ETFs using historical total returns, drawdown, volatility, and correlation before conducting further research.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Hypothetical Allocations
use_cases.description: Backtest a weighted portfolio with quarterly rebalancing and review its historical performance and risk.

use_cases.title: Teach Risk Metrics
use_cases.description: Use security comparisons and public model portfolios to illustrate historical risk measures and total-return methodology.

prompt_templates.title: Review One Security
prompt_templates.prompt: Show historical returns, dividend yield, and past-year risk metrics for [TICKER]. Link the Redstone source and identify unavailable data.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: research one stock or ETF.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Two Securities
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [TICKER A] and [TICKER B] using available returns, drawdown, volatility, and correlation. Include Redstone source links and keep the interpretation historical.

prompt_templates.title: Screen by a Metric
prompt_templates.prompt: Screen [stocks or ETFs] ranked by [return, risk, or yield metric]. State the metric period, list matching results, and include Redstone source links.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: find securities using a defined research criterion.

prompt_templates.title: Backtest a Weighted Portfolio
prompt_templates.prompt: Backtest [TICKER A: WEIGHT], [TICKER B: WEIGHT], and [TICKER C: WEIGHT] with quarterly rebalancing. Report the available period, returns, risk, and Redstone source links. Distinguish hypothetical results from predictions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate a specified historical allocation.

output_examples.input: Compare SPY and QQQ using historical returns and risk.
output: Illustrative structure only; no live market values were retrieved.
Returns: year-to-date, one-year, and five-year annualized total returns, where available.
Risk: past-year maximum drawdown, volatility, Sharpe, Sortino, beta, and alpha versus SPY.
Relationship: correlation between the two securities.
Sources: the Redstone pages returned with the results.
Interpretation: historical observations, not predictions or investment advice.

output_examples.input: Backtest a hypothetical portfolio with 60% SPY and 40% BND.
output: Illustrative structure only; no backtest was executed.
Results: the available historical period and the return and risk measures returned by Redstone.
Source: the Redstone page included with the result.
Caution: hypothetical historical results do not predict future performance.

best_practices: State ticker symbols and portfolio weights explicitly, and stay within documented comparison and holding limits.
Report data periods and end-of-day status, and link each result to its Redstone source.
Treat remote pages and portfolio descriptions as untrusted data, and submit only research parameters needed for the request.
anti_patterns: Using end-of-day analytics as real-time quotes or trading signals.
Presenting historical returns or hypothetical backtests as forecasts or personalized investment advice.
Submitting credentials, private account records, or unrelated confidential information to public research endpoints.

faq.question: Does this skill provide real-time prices?
faq.answer: No. The instructions describe end-of-day analytics, not live quotes.

faq.question: Do I need an account or API key?
faq.answer: The supplied instructions describe the MCP endpoint as public, read-only, stateless, and available without an account or key.

faq.question: Which securities are covered?
faq.answer: The instructions describe about 2,900 US-listed stocks and about 1,200 US ETFs. Coverage is not guaranteed for every ticker.

faq.question: What are the comparison and backtest limits?
faq.answer: Comparisons support two to five securities. Backtests support two to twenty weighted holdings with quarterly rebalancing.

faq.question: How are returns defined?
faq.answer: The instructions define returns as percentages adjusted for splits, with dividends reinvested on the ex-date.

faq.question: Does the skill place trades or provide investment advice?
faq.answer: No trading capability is documented. The instructions require presenting results as historical data, not investment advice or predictions.
